content:
alex: :rotating_light: emergency — I just applied a manual model pin to us-west-2 to force traffic onto `model-x-q4` after a latency spike. Seeing immediate 502/timeout spike and a routing fallback churn across regions. not good.
incidents-bot: Incident created — Sev2 (auto) — SmartRoutingFallback loop detected for service: inference-api. thread: 2128501234. Pager alerting oncall.
sam: oncall here, looking. can you paste the exact command you ran? need to understand if this was a hard pin or a routing hint.
alex: ran: ```redwood ctl route pin --region us-west-2 --model model-x-q4 --force``` thought it was a temporary pin for canary. wanted to drain old variant, but may have mis-specified the variant id.
mike: seeing repeated global fallbacks in the routing logs — requests go to us-west-2 -> errors -> fallback to eu-west-1 -> then routing policy re-evaluates and sends back to us-west-2. it's oscillating every ~30s.
irene: paging in case. I'm the current infra oncall — taking this. who's owning comms? cs-lead please tag impacted customers.
cs-lead: Customer impact: three enterprise tenants showing increased latencies and 12-18% error rates on generation endpoints. One is in SLO breach window. Notifying account owners now. We'll prepare an incident bridge note.
henry: Quick thought — did the model variant have a different tokenizer/kv-cache format? cross-variant cache mismatch can trigger runtime errors and client-side retries, which the router treats as failures and triggers fallback.
alex: yup, `model-x-q4` is quantized with a different kv-layout than the previous `model-x-v2`. I expected runtime to handle compatibility but maybe not for the pinned path.
deploy-bot: Deploy log: rollback started for routing policy  /policies/smart-route-1 by alex at 2128501310.
sam: ok, do NOT fully rollback the policy yet. we need a controlled unwind. if we unpin abruptly, traffic may get stuck to old variant due to sticky session keys. we saw this causing sticky loops previously.
irene: agreed. plan: 1) reduce traffic to us-west-2 by 50% via weight shift, 2) disable auto-fallback for 2 mins, 3) unpin after KV flush. any objections?
mike: how do we flush KV caches across the fleet? any safe command? routers expect cache TTL to expire which could be minutes.
alex: there is a drain command — `redwood runtime drain-cache --model model-x-q4 --region us-west-2 --force` but that only flushes local caches. need to run in a rolling fashion across pods.
irene: I'll start a controlled weight shift now. executing: ```redwood ctl route set-weight --policy smart-route-1 --region us-west-2 --weight 50 --reason "control unwind"``` will monitor.
incidents-bot: Action logged by irene: route weight change (us-west-2 -> 50%).
mike: logs: after weight shift, error rate dropped from 18% -> 9% but latency still elevated for some customers.
henry: any evicted connections or stateful pods that kept stale KV? check pod restarts.
sam: mike, can you run `kubectl get pods -l app=inference -n prod -o wide` and grep for crashloop or restart counts?
mike: ```bash
kubectl get pods -l app=inference -n prod -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
inference-ss-0    0
inference-ss-1    3
inference-ss-2    0
inference-ss-3    4
``` those two with restarts coincide with nodes in us-west-2.
alex: I also see router logs with `variant_mismatch_error: KV_FORMAT_MISMATCH` and the fallback counter increments. that's the root cause.
cs-lead: updating customers: "We're investigating elevated errors; temporary mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with timeline and postmortem." :thumbsup:
irene: next step: stop auto-fallback for the policy so it doesn't keep oscillating. command: ```redwood ctl policy update smart-route-1 --auto-fallback false --reason "stabilize while we drain"``` executing now.
incidents-bot: Policy smart-route-1 auto-fallback: disabled by irene at 2128501540.
sam: good. now let's drain the quantized variant pods in us-west-2, one at a time, then unpin. mike, schedule drain:
mike: running: ```redwood runtime drain-pods --model model-x-q4 --region us-west-2 --concurrency 1 --wait 60s``` starting.
deploy-bot: Drain initiated: 8 pods targeted in us-west-2. linear rollout.
mike: draining first pod — traffic offloaded, no 5xx spikes. proceeding.
alex: while draining, we should patch the runtime to accept both kv formats but that is risky mid-incident. postpone to postmortem.
henry: agree — too risky.
cs-lead: customer A's SLA hit window ends in 22mins. need an estimate for resolution.
irene: timeline: weight shift done, auto-fallback off, drain in progress. if drains complete without errors we'll unpin and set weight back in ~12-15 minutes.
sam: mike — any signs of sticky session keys still routing to drained pods? check request ids vs pod ids.
mike: not seeing new requests to drained pods after offload. error rate trending down to ~4% for most customers except one noisy tenant.
cs-lead: notifying the noisy tenant's CSM and offering a temporary routing bypass to eu-west-1 if they want immediate relief.
alex: ok prepping the unpin command: ```redwood ctl route unpin --region us-west-2 --policy smart-route-1 --model model-x-q4 --reason "post-drain unwind"``` will hold until drain success.
incidents-bot: Drain progress: 6/8 pods drained — no new variant_mismatch errors in last 60s.
mike: 8/8 drained. I'm ready to unpin when you give the go.
irene: go for unpin, but keep weight at 50% for another 2 minutes, then gradually restore.
alex: executing unpin now.
deploy-bot: Route unpin executed by alex at 2128501899. change id: ch_9a8b.
sam: monitor for stickiness. if we see re-routes back and forth, enable circuit-breaker on that policy.
mike: checking traces — sticky keys resolved. fallback churn stopped. error rates back to baseline for two tenants; one tenant still at 7% but we have a mitigation plan with CSM.
cs-lead: customers notified. ticket updates posted. no new escalations.
irene: handing off oncall back to sam in 10 mins. summary for postmortem: manual forced pin to quantized variant with incompatible KV format triggered runtime errors -> smart routing auto-fallback oscillated across regions -> attempted immediate rollback would have caused sticky routing; we performed controlled weight shift, disabled auto-fallback, drained pods, unpinned, and restored weights. root cause candidate: lack of compatibility checks on model variant pins and missing preflight for KV layout.
sam: taking over. annotate follow-ups: 1) add variant-compatibility preflight in ctl pin, 2) add a 'safe-unpin' orchestration that does weight shifts & cache drains, 3) improve observability: tie KV_FORMAT_MISMATCH to alerting and SLO impact.
henry: also: make auto-fallback aware of pin operations (suppress during manual pin/unpin windows).
alex: +1 on all. I'll open the postmortem draft and own the RCA. thanks everyone for the quick coordination.
incidents-bot: Incident 2128501234 resolved -> monitoring mode. Total duration: 16344s? (placeholder) Please update resolution details and severity in the incident tracker.
cs-lead: will file customer post-incident summary and runbook entries. :white_check_mark:
irene: releasing oncall to sam. handing over notes in #eng-oncall. :handshake:
sam: ack — will follow up on runbook updates and move to retro. closing bridge in 15.
alex: closing thread notes here. thanks all. :heart:
